# 07 Ship a browser bundle and a clickable step-reveal demo page

## Outcome

`pnpm --filter @siren/core build` produces a browser-consumable library bundle (Vite library
mode), and `demos/step-reveal.html` loads that real bundle, calls `render()` with an example
flowchart + timeline, and wires "Next" / "Reset" buttons to the returned controller — a human
opening the page in a browser can watch nodes fade in one step at a time.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `pnpm --filter @siren/core build` exits 0 and produces a browser-loadable output (ESM and/or
  IIFE) under `packages/core/dist/`.
- [ ] `demos/step-reveal.html` imports that built bundle (not source files), defines an example
  Siren document with at least 3 nodes across 2+ timeline steps, and calls `render()` on page load.
- [ ] The page has visible "Next" and "Reset" buttons; clicking "Next" calls `controller.next()`
  and the corresponding node(s) visibly fade in (CSS transition on `siren-enter-fade`, defined in
  a shipped stylesheet); clicking "Reset" calls `controller.reset()` and the diagram returns to
  its initial state.
- [ ] Opening `demos/step-reveal.html` directly in a browser (or via a static file server) shows
  the flowchart correctly laid out with no console errors.

## Test seam

Manual/visual verification in a real browser — this is the ticket the earlier "do we want a
browser demo" decision was for. The build step itself (`pnpm --filter @siren/core build` exits 0,
expected output files exist) is mechanically checkable; the animation's visual correctness is
confirmed by a human, not an automated assertion, in this slice. Automated browser e2e (Playwright)
is explicitly deferred per the spec's non-goals.
